title: Introduce adaptive syntactic-variance detector CI hook and lightweight perturbation probe
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Flaky regressions and QA noise often stem from increased syntactic sensitivity even when semantic fidelity remains stable. This PR adds an adaptive syntactic-variance detector CI hook plus a lightweight perturbation probe that generates syntactic paraphrases (word-order swaps, passive/active transform, small connective insertions) and computes a syntactic-variance score per prompt. The detector compares current-run distributions to an historical baseline using a robust bootstrap and applies a context-conditioned threshold: prompt groups with stable semantic eval scores but rising syntactic variance will be flagged for review while noisy prompts can be quarantined. Implementation notes: the hook is implemented as an optional eval-harness plugin (SyntacticVarianceProbe), a small perturbation engine (rules+randomized templates), and a CI adapter that emits JSON decision blobs compatible with existing gating machinery. This PR includes a migration script to generate initial baselines from the last 30 runs and a smoke test suite. Checklist: [x] core probe implementation, [x] CI adapter + gate integration, [x] baseline backfill script, [x] unit and integration tests, [x] docs and example config. Expected behavioral changes: new CI failures only when syntactic variance exceeds adaptive thresholds for >=2 consecutive runs; no change to semantic SLO gating. Related Linear: ENG-1589, ENG-1622.

release_notes: Adds a syntactic-variance CI hook that detects increased sensitivity to syntactic perturbations for prompt sets and quarantines noisy prompts. Configurable and opt-in via eval-harness plugins.
testing_summary: Unit tests: syntactic probe rules, parser heuristics and adapter mapping covered. Integration: end-to-end simulated CI run with mock model outputs across 5 cohorts; baseline backfill validated. Performance: probe adds ~30ms per prompt in local mode; disabled in batch runs by default. CI matrix: linux-py39 unit+integration passed on all runners after one flaky test fix.
review_comments: Rohit Patel: Overall this looks good. Two concerns: 1) the perturbation engine uses heuristics that might bias certain languages—can we guard the probe with locale tags? 2) the bootstrap alpha is 0.05 hardcoded in the adapter; make it configurable.
Maya Chen (author): Addressed both. Added locale guard and config param 'syntactic_variance.bootstrap_alpha' with default 0.05; updated docs and tests to cover non-English prompt skip behavior.
Evelyn Soto: Tests are comprehensive. Request: add a small note in docs about false positives during model warm-up and suggest a grace window for new cohorts.
Maya Chen (author): Added guidance in docs and implemented a grace-window option 'cohort_grace_runs' that defaults to 2 runs. Will follow up with telemetry to monitor false-positive rate.
Arun Mehta: Minor nit: use consistent logging keys for probe outputs so downstream alerting can pick them up. Also call out expected extra latency in the CI gating docs.
Maya Chen (author): Normalized logging keys to 'syntactic_variance.score' and 'syntactic_variance.delta'; updated ci_gates.md with performance notes.
notes_on_deployment: Opt-in via eval-harness config; to enable add 'plugins: [syntactic_variance]' and configure thresholds. Backfill script should be run once per workspace to seed baselines. Recommended rollout: enable in canary CI first, monitor false-positive rate for two weeks, then flip to full CI gating.
risk_assessment: Low-medium. The probe is deterministic and opt-in; false positives are possible for morphologically rich languages. We mitigate by locale skipping, grace window, and requiring consecutive-run exceedance before gating. No runtime change to model serving.
author_affirmations: I have run unit and integration tests locally and validated baseline backfill against the last 30 runs. I confirm no semantic gating behavior was modified by this change.
human_readable_summary: Adds an eval-harness plugin that measures how much a prompt's output changes under syntactic-only perturbations and wires that signal into an adaptive CI gate to detect regressions caused by syntactic sensitivity increases. Configurable, documented, and accompanied by tests and a baseline backfill script.
